We ran the three profiles this morning (attached acme_concurrency_results_1129.csv). Summary:
- Burst probe (2m): observed large queue-depth spikes ~40-45s into the run leading to TTFT jumps from ~120ms p50 to ~1.8s p99.

Thanks for the data, Tom — good notes and very helpful CSV. Quick analysis and immediate mitigations:

1) Burst probe p99 spikes — likely queueing induced by kernel scheduling and a cold KV-cache (prefix misses). Short-term mitigations:
   - Enable aggressive prefix/KV pre-warming for the first 60s of the burst; this reduced p99 by ~40% in our internal repros.
   - Add a soft admission control at the proxy with a 200ms queue-time cutoff to shed excess requests in the 2nd minute of the burst.

2) Steady-state micro-pauses — looks like a cache thrash pattern tied to your request routing (worker affinity). Suggestions:
   - Use sticky routing for 30s windows to increase KV cache locality.
   - Tune your steady-state limiter to a slightly higher short-window burst (e.g., 700 req/s) to avoid frequent small backoffs that cause uneven worker load.

3) Endurance memory pressure — we saw similar behaviour in a test job last quarter after long context-length burns. Short-term:
   - Decrease per-request max_tokens by 10% for endurance runs to reduce peak mem.
   - Run the endurance job with two workers to spread KV state.

I've attached a candidate rate_limit_suggestions.yml with concrete values and a short canary ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100% traffic over 3 hours) for deploying the tuned policy. Also linking our internal runbook for queueing diagnostics: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PerfMAPdocs (shared view).

If you're open, we can run a mirrored burst probe from Redwood staging tomorrow morning and share the full trace so we can line up the timestamps. Marissa — can you confirm the canary calendar and I will prepare the rollout steps?
